📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, MP3 — short for Music Presentation 3 — just dropped its second episode, and with it fresh laughs and wild tracks. As Dropout's first scripted series in seven years, this music video countdown show parodies MTV's long-canceled Total Request Live. As such, MP3 offers quirky VJs and three new music videos each episode.

Saturday Night Live's Jeremy Culhane plays Dane Cartel, a former boy-bander/host with "lightly bad behavior," who is joined by newly minted VJs Dr. Muse-Tina (Skye Townsend) and Chia (Aparna Nancherla).

In a recent development, behind the music are MP3 co-creators and the podcast Off Book hosts, Zach Reino and Jess McKenna, who penned nine original songs across a wide range of genres for the season. From their long-running improvised emo outfit Every Place I Cry (alongside Nick Mandernach and Ross Bryant) to Joe Cocker-style vocals from Jacob Wysocki, the series showcases real singing from Dropout's roster—including Dropout CEO Sam Reich, Elaine Carroll, and even a surpising cameo from Paul Robalino (aka Paul Refereeno). Plus, the show is packed with Dropout Cinematic Universe Easter eggs, pulling in Smartypants callbacks ("No Thank You, the Ocean") and Very Notable People's Princess Emily.

Mashable's Entertainment Editor, Kristy Puchko, sat down with Reino and McKenna in a virtual interview to learn how MP3 came together, why they never mock the music genres they parody, and the real reason a character's face is blurred out in the trailer.

In a recent development, how to watch: The first two episodes of MP3 are streaming now on Dropout, with the season finale on Dec. 2. #59437. El Niño Is Driving a Record Marine Heat Wave Off the California Coast

El Niño Is Driving a Record Marine Heat Wave Off the California Coast

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (810 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that for the past 20 years, Daniel Rudnick has been collecting data from below the ocean’s surface.
  • The oceanographer helps to pilot small underwater drones known as gliders that dive thousands of feet below the surface and crawl their way back up, collecting data on salinity, temperature, and other metrics.
  • A color-coded chart showing temperature anomalies at different depths in the ocean—red for hotter, blue for colder—had to be readjusted because the red shades weren’t intense enough to accurately reflect just how hot things are, even hundreds of meters below the surface.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for the past 20 years, Daniel Rudnick has been collecting data from below the ocean’s surface. He’s never seen anything like what’s been coming back for the past few months, as a super El Niño fuels record heat off the California coast. The marine heat wave is affecting wildlife and helping to juice the record-setting storms hitting the state at the start of the rainy season.

The oceanographer helps to pilot small underwater drones known as gliders that dive thousands of feet below the surface and crawl their way back up, collecting data on salinity, temperature, and other metrics.

A color-coded chart showing temperature anomalies at different depths in the ocean—red for hotter, blue for colder—had to be readjusted because the red shades weren’t intense enough to accurately reflect just how hot things are, even hundreds of meters below the surface. Steric height—changes to sea levels driven by heat rather than melting ice—has reached the highest levels Rudnick has ever seen.

“I looked back at our data to make sure that I'm not making a mistake and it's correct—and it is,” Rudnick, who works at the Scripps Institution of Oceanography at UC San Diego, says.

In Monterey Bay, a station recorded a temperature of 64.72 degrees Fahrenheit (18.18 degrees Celsius) at a depth of 200 feet below the water’s surface in late October, breaking previous records. Other data highlights even hotter water in San Diego at the same depth: 77 degrees Fahrenheit, an anomaly of 21.3 degrees Fahrenheit above normal.

Recent findings suggest that el Niño “is the biggest source of climate variability” off the California coast, Rudnick says. The climate phenomenon is characterized by hotter-than-normal water in the eastern tropical Pacific and affects weather and oceans around the globe. His gliders have captured temperature anomalies across other events, including intense heat during the 2015–2016 super El Niño. But this year’s El Niño is shaping up to be the strongest on record, and its impacts are equally supersized.

“It’s fair to say it’s off the charts,” he notes.

Sources indicate that this year’s El Niño is adding heat to an already-simmering ocean. Since January 2025, coastal California waters have been hit by a massive heat wave, with temperatures in some places reaching 8 degrees Fahrenheit above average in August. Add in human-caused climate change—oceans off Southern California have warmed 1.8 degrees Fahrenheit since the 1970s alone—and it makes for unprecedented conditions now.

“This is a bunch of things that have had to come together to make this even physically possible,” Daniel Swain, a climate scientist at the University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources, indicates. “And even then, it's kind of astonishing.”.

It has been revealed that rudnick agrees. “The heat we get from El Niño stacking on top of the heat we already have, that’s the thing that makes this most unusual,” he notes.

In a recent development, part of what’s driving the higher ocean temperatures and sea levels off California are what’s known as Kelvin waves. These slow, large waves transport warm water from west to east across the Pacific. They in turn push down the ocean’s thermocline, a transition layer into the deeper ocean where temperatures begin to decrease rapidly.

“It isn't like there's some heater in the deep ocean suddenly,” Swain says. “It's just that we've turned off the air conditioner and we're allowing the surface waters to warm.”.

Kelvin waves can also help to raise sea levels along the California coast by “keeping the water from moving physically offshore,” Swain notes. While Kelvin waves are imperceptible to the average person, their impacts aren’t.

In a recent development, californians have been living through several weeks of intense coastal flooding and big waves enhanced by these higher sea levels. San Francisco and the surrounding area are under a coastal flood advisory through Friday morning, and waves have reached over 30 feet (9 meters) in height and even set off seismographs. (Another storm is set to hit the Bay Area this weekend.) It’s also contributing to heavier rainfall, with locations from San Francisco to Burbank setting hourly rainfall records in recent days.

But the warmer water itself is also contributing to this temporary sea level rise, thanks to simple physics: Warmer water takes up more space, helping push up sea levels.

The warm water is driving weather even more unprecedented than the intense storms. On Tuesday, two rare twin waterspouts formed over San Francisco Bay, the result of cold storm air moving over unusually warm waters. These phenomena are generally seen off the coast of Florida or the Mediterranean—not in the usually frigid waters of the Pacific.

According to recent reports, “The air temperatures are somewhat winter-like right now, but the water ain't,” Swain notes. “It’s an indicator that things aren’t as they usually are in this part of the world.”.

#59436. Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal

Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (900 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Two years of fan pressure and criticism has forced Borussia Dortmund to drop a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer, Rheinmetall.
  • Industry observers note that the Bundesliga club will not renew its deal with Rheinmetall beyond its expiry in June 2027, at the end of this season.
  • Industry observers note that "It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two years of fan pressure and criticism has forced Borussia Dortmund to drop a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer, Rheinmetall.

Industry observers note that the Bundesliga club will not renew its deal with Rheinmetall beyond its expiry in June 2027, at the end of this season. Dortmund chairman Carsten Cramer confirmed the news on the club's website ahead of its AGM on Sunday, which may have proved a potential flashpoint. He acknowledged that "our partnership has been controversial from the outset" but lamented the loss of income.

Industry observers note that "It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre. We will have to reprioritize planned investments and carefully examine how we can find viable solutions.".

Though he welcomed the news, one of the leaders of the fan revolt against the partnership, Michael Schulze von Glaser, warned this is likely not the end of the road.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, "I think in the end it was a victory for the fans. But I'm also a bit skeptical about  what the future will bring us," the Dortmund fan and former head of the German Peace Society told DW. "Football fans in Germany always must be skeptical and always must watch what the club is doing.”.

In a recent development, many Dortmund fans have opposed the deal — which has seen Rheinmetall's logo on advertising boards and other surfaces at locations such as Dortmund's 83,000-capacity Westfalenstadion — from its beginnings in 2024. It was estimated to be worth between €7 ($7.68 million) and €9 million per year.

Sources indicate that at the club's AGM that year, 556 of 855 members present voted against the deal in a non-binding vote. There were 247 votes in favour, with 52 abstentions. This, said Cramer, informed the eventual outcome.

Rheinmetall sells arms mostly to Germany, Ukraine and NATO but fans and critics feel that platforming any arms manufacturer goes against the club's statement of its core values. In that, Dortmund states its desire for "a club and a society that operate free of racism, anti-Semitism, LGBTQIA+ hostility, sexism, violence and discrimination.".

To play this audio please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 audio.

It has always been clear, remarked Schulze von Glaser, that this deal did not chime with that.

"In the end, they kill people. They are for war," he said of Rheinmetall. "The slogan of Borussia Dortmund is true love (Echte Liebe). But for me and many others, our love ends there…. I know some fans who have put fan merchandise in the trash because they were so shocked.”.

Industry observers note that in the Q and A on the club's website, Cramer noted he was still a "personal advocate" of the deal but that Dortmund's commitment to the 50+1 model, which means German clubs are majority controlled by the members, meant they had to listen to fan voices. But he also warned that Rheinmetall must be an "absolute exception and an isolated case.".

That set off some alarm bells for Schulze von Glaser.

"It's a bit concerning that there are constantly these attacks on professional football — a new sponsorship, investment deals," he said.

Indeed, Dortmund's climbdown is not the first of its kind in Germany's top flight. Last year, after fan and media pressure, Bayern Munich ended its commercial deal with the tourism arm of the Rwandan government before its conclusion.

Fans had objected to the promotion of Rwanda, which many felt sought to divert attention from its poor human rights record and actions in the war with DR Congo, through sporting partnerships. Two years earlier, Bayern withdrew from a similarly controversial deal with Qatar Airways.

Elsewhere in the league, Werder Bremen fans objected to their long time shirt sponsor, Wiesenhof. Many supporters took problem with the factory farming practices  of Germany's largest poultry producer. Though it was not given as a direct reason for the end of a shirt sponsorship deal in 2023, it likely played a part.

Union Berlin fans have also made their voices heard. When the club signed a newly introduced shirt-sponsorship deal with Luxembourg real estate organization, Aroundtown, upon promotion to the top flight in 2019, many fans were frustrated at the tie up in a city where rent prices were skyrocketing.

"It's a problem for a lot of people," fan Sven Dobberstein told DW at the time.

"We have to try to find a way between commercialization and what we have at the moment. It isn't easy.".

Recent findings suggest that striking that balance can often be a source of tension for Bundesliga clubs. 50+1 ensures fans have a voice, preventing rich owners, or nation states, from taking control as they do in England's lucrative Premier League or in France or Spain. Indeed fan protests have also stopped the league signing a €1billion private equity partner and seen Monday night matches scrapped. For Schulze von Glaser, this needs to be protected.

"In Germany, the fan culture has an impact," he said.

”If there is something bad or terrible happening in your club and in the Bundesliga, there are the organized fans and they can have an impact if they want, if they stand together and, yes, they can stop the Rheinmetall deal.".

Additional reporting by: Emmie Eernisse.

HSBC's top execs face tense shareholders calling for a breakup

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 5 min read (992 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • HSBC’s top brass defended their strategy Monday to frustrated shareholders in the lender’s largest market, as Europe’s biggest bank continued to face calls to be split up.
  • At an informal shareholder meeting in Hong Kong, Chairman Mark Tucker and CEO Noel Quinn took questions from investors on concerns ranging from how the bank was approaching demands for an overhaul of its business to its purchase of Silicon Valley Bank’s UK arm.
  • In prepared remarks, Tucker and Quinn each reiterated the board’s recommendation that shareholders vote against a resolution on the docket for its annual general meeting in May that would force the bank to come up with a plan to spin off or reorganize its Asian business — the lender’s main source of profits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HSBC’s top brass defended their strategy Monday to frustrated shareholders in the lender’s largest market, as Europe’s biggest bank continued to face calls to be split up.

At an informal shareholder meeting in Hong Kong, Chairman Mark Tucker and CEO Noel Quinn took questions from investors on concerns ranging from how the bank was approaching demands for an overhaul of its business to its purchase of Silicon Valley Bank’s UK arm.

In prepared remarks, Tucker and Quinn each reiterated the board’s recommendation that shareholders vote against a resolution on the docket for its annual general meeting in May that would force the bank to come up with a plan to spin off or reorganize its Asian business — the lender’s main source of profits.

HSBC's biggest shareholder reignites debate about breaking up the bank.

Tucker remarked the board was unanimous in its opposition to the resolution, stating plainly: “It would not be in your interest to split the bank.”.

He stated the board had previously reviewed a range of options for restructuring the bank, and concluded that such alternatives would “materially destroy value for shareholders,” including dividends.

According to recent reports, “Our strategy is working,” Tucker told the room of more than 1,000 shareholders. “Our current strategy is moving dividends up.”.

HSBC has been facing calls to separate its Asian business from the rest of the bank over the past year.

Shareholders in Hong Kong — where HSBC is a mainstay of many retail investors’ portfolios — contend that the London-based lender’s performance has been dragged down by its businesses in other regions.

Quinn addressed those complaints head-on Monday, saying “our profits in Hong Kong and the UK are no longer being dragged down by underperformance elsewhere. The group is performing well as a whole.”.

Pressed later by a shareholder on the glitch, Quinn said a breakup of the bank would result in “significant revenue loss” because much of its business relied on cross-border transactions.

Investors have also been unhappy with HSBC scrapping its dividend in 2020, at the request of British regulators. They argue that if the lender cordoned off its activities in Asia, it would no longer have to expose Hong Kong shareholders to requests in other jurisdictions.

Christine Fong, a district council member in Hong Kong, noted she represented about 500 small shareholders who had been affected by the dividend cancellation.

“Street hawkers, taxi drivers or teachers — they all relied on the dividend to pay for their regular expenses, like mortgage, insurance payments, school fees,” Fong told CNN.

“That’s why, three years ago, what HSBC did upset those small minority shareholders.”.

Fong has now joined calls for shareholders to vote in favor of the proposal for the bank to spin off its Asian business, despite the lender bringing back its dividend in 2021, albeit at a lower level.

Ken Lui, an activist shareholder in Hong Kong who put the resolution together, doubled down on his call for support ahead of the meeting Monday.

The resolution will require 75% of votes to be passed in May, but “nothing is impossible,” he told reporters outside the meeting venue.

Lui, who noted he personally held a stake worth 100 million Hong Kong dollars ($12.7 million), laid out plans for his team to focus on “targeted outreach to institutional shareholders to present our case and gain their support.”.

His group will also canvass 18 districts of Hong Kong “to tell HSBC shareholders that they finally have a chance to speak for themselves and protect their rights through voting,” he added.

HSBC is also facing pressure from its largest shareholder.

Ping An (PNGAY), China’s biggest insurer, holds an 8% stake in HSBC and has backed calls for the bank to rethink its structure.

In a series of remarks made public by the Chinese firm last November, Huang Yong, chairman of Ping An’s asset management arm, stated “we will support any initiatives including a spinoff that are conducive to improve HSBC’s performance and value.”.

Since then, the insurance giant’s views haven’t changed, according to a person familiar with the matter.

The source told CNN that Ping An has been calling for HSBC to explore a reorganization, with an eye on boosting its valuation and simplifying its regulatory obligations around the globe.

According to recent reports, the insurer has not recommended a specific path forward but will support any initiatives, including a spinoff of its Asian business, that could boost its stock performance or value, the person added. Ping An did not immediately respond to a request for comment on how it planned to vote at the upcoming general meeting.

It has been revealed that HSBC’s leaders were also asked Monfday why the bank had scooped up the British unit of SVB following the stunning collapse of its parent in the United States. The purchase was made for £1 ($1.20) last month, just days after SVB had folded.

Critics have questioned HSBC’s ability to perform adequate due diligence on SVB UK’s customers because of how promptly the deal came together.

“Did HSBC look into the clients of SVB in detail? Say, the financial statement — whether they can pay back the loan?” said Fong.

HSBC buys SVB's UK business, ending 'nightmare' for British tech.

Quinn and Tucker defended the acquisition, calling it a good business opportunity that allowed the bank to gain hundreds of innovative startups as customers. They pushed back on the notion that management hadn’t had time to carry out proper due diligence.

Tucker also weighed in on recent tumult in the banking industry, saying he did not expect an “immediate impact” on HSBC.

“After the collapse of a number of smaller regional banks and the takeover of Credit Suisse, the share prices of all banks have been suppressed,” he noted.

But he said he did not believe such developments represented “a systemic risk” to the sector. “I do expect a period of uncertainty” before nerves settle, he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Celtic 4-1 St Mirren; Rangers 2-1 Motherwell.

Wouter Vrancken noted Hearts’ remarkable 8-0 demolition of 10-man Dundee was his team’s best performance since he took charge at Tynecastle.

Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kaboré both scored twice with Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Stuart Findlay and a Ryan Finnigan own goal completing the rout. Vrancken was naturally delighted that his players had ended a run of three defeats in a row in such spectacular style.

According to recent reports, “Our best performance? Of course,” he said. “When you have the confidence of one moment and then you feel the score is getting bigger, you see the players with extra confidence. You see the dynamics there and it’s good they feel it works.

“It was ruthless and I like to see it this way. That was the message at half-time – that and keeping the clean sheet. But it’s only the first step, only one game and we have to try to bring more.”.

Steven Pressley admitted he was embarrassed by the result and Dundee’s performance, saying: “It’s a night I need to own, a night where I can only apologise for the performance. I never expected that.

“I had a little sense we haven’t been quite on it over the last couple of weeks but I take ownership and I mean that. We talk about the culture and environment that we set and part of that is making sure we have a fully motivated team, a team which works hard and demonstrates grit. We didn’t show that tonight but that is on me and I mean that. I’m embarrassed by it and I accept it.”.

Recent findings suggest that the recalled midfielders Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan both scored as Celtic beat St Mirren 4-1. The champions brushed off the loss of midfield pair Mika Baur and Benjamin Nygren to injury to consolidate their place at the top of the Premiership.

The centre-forward Camilo Duran was also on target as Celtic killed the game late in the first half with three goals in nine minutes. Callum McGregor grabbed his first league goal of the season before Killian Phillips scored a consolation from the spot.

With Baur facing up to 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Nygren nursing a heel problem, Martin O’Neill would have been delighted with how his midfield functioned.

Oxlade-Chamberlain made his fifth start of the season and McCowan his second. The pair had never started a game together before. O’Neill also introduced the former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joël van den Berg for a debut in the second half and the 19-year-old demonstrated some good touches.

Ryan Naderi hit a deflected 88th-minute winner at Fir Park as Rangers stayed four points behind Celtic by beating Motherwell 2-1. Naderi’s effort went in off the unfortunate Motherwell defender Martin Moorman as Rangers finally made the most of some late pressure to win.

The visitors looked as if they might be held to a third draw in four away games after Jake Girdwood-Reich had cancelled out an early opener from Rangers defender Emmanuel Fernandez. Rangers had 29 shots at goal but found Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen in top form and the New Zealand international pulled off one of the saves of the season to deny Dujon Sterling with five minutes left.

However, they netted after a corner when Naderi’s shot from eight yards went in off Moorman after the Austrian had blocked a shot from Badredine Bouanani.

It has been revealed that mario Frick enjoyed a dream start to life as Aberdeen manager by edging a six-goal thriller with a 4-2 win at Kilmarnock. Kevin Nisbet’s double along with Brad Lyons and Findlay Marshall strikes secured three priceless points to leave the Rugby Park side rooted to the bottom.

The visitors climbed to eighth spot after a remarkable afternoon where the Pittodrie side hit a much-needed scoring streak. Aberdeen opted to dispense with the services of Stephen Robinson after a run of one win from seven which saw them sink to second bottom and Frick was appointed as his replacement last Sunday.

It has been revealed that dundee United recorded their biggest ever win at Easter Road with an impressive 4-0 thrashing of Hibernian. Zac Sapsford’s first-half double laid the foundations before Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall found the net after the break.

The visitors were well worth the three points as they cemented their place in the top six and picked up their first win in Leith since 2021. It was a humbling afternoon for Hibs, who thought they had turned a corner under their upcoming head coach, Marink Reedijk, after back-to-back victories before the international break.

Falkirk clung on to clock up six top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1966 with a 2-1 home victory against St Johnstone. John McGlynn’s team scored early in each half to remain third.

It has been revealed that jacob Murrell’s eighth goal of a superb debut season sent Falkirk on their way inside six minutes. Finley Barbrook’s second goal in as many games on 48 minutes doubled the advantage. Josh Campbell nodded in a late reply to serve up a scare but the hosts held firm.

It has been revealed that if you are holding out for Black Friday on Nov. 27 to finally buy a PlayStation 5, it is time to set some realistic expectations.

Last year's Black Friday sale was a banner event for Sony shoppers, bringing $100+ markdowns and free pack-in games across almost the entire lineup. Between a global RAM shortage that pushed Sony to raise console prices and the launch of GTA 6, deep standalone console discounts are largely off the table. That does not mean you cannot save money on PlayStation gear during Thanksgiving week — you just have to know where the real deals will show up.

Industry observers note that driven by rising memory costs from the AI boom and supply chain pressures, Sony officially raised U.S. retail prices across its entire console lineup on April 2. Today, the PS5 Slim Digital Edition starts at $599.99, the PS5 Slim Disc Edition sits at $649.99, and the flagship PS5 Pro retails for $899.99.

Recent findings suggest that even if Sony or major retailers like Walmart, Best Buy, and Target shave $50 to $100 off a PS5 Slim during Black Friday week, those sale prices will simply bring the console back down to what it used to cost before April. Meanwhile, standalone discounts on the PS5 Pro look practically nonexistent.

According to recent reports, the Pro is already largely sold out across major U.S. stores ahead of GTA 6 launch day, so a realistic Black Friday "win" for Pro shoppers is simply catching an official restock at regular list price rather than paying third-party reseller markups.

In a recent development, if Sony does anything for PS5 consoles during Black Friday week, expect game bundles rather than raw price cuts. Sony loves keeping the console at full sticker price while tossing in a free pack-in game voucher — which is nice if you wanted the game anyway, but not much help if you just want a cheaper console. Nonprofit Common Space will launch 1st 'humanitarian satellite' in 2027

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The nonprofit Common Space plans to assemble a six-spacecraft constellation of Earth-observing satellites, whose high-resolution imagery will aid first responders, journalists, scientists and human-rights investigators around the world.
  • It has been revealed that that strategy firmed up a bit today (Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first satellite in a constellation designed for humanitarian use will lift off next year, if all goes according to initiative.

The nonprofit Common Space plans to assemble a six-spacecraft constellation of Earth-observing satellites, whose high-resolution imagery will aid first responders, journalists, scientists and human-rights investigators around the world.

It has been revealed that that strategy firmed up a bit today (Nov. 19), as Common Space unveiled the builder of the first of those satellites: Satellogic, an Argentine-U.S. geospatial intelligence tech giant.

Sources indicate that there are more than 1,000 Earth-observing satellites circling our planet at the moment. But much of the data they gather is proprietary or too expensive to serve the common good, according to Common Space.

The nonprofit wants to change that via its envisioned constellation, which it states will collect imagery specifically for humanitarian and public-interest purposes. Common Space prepares to operate on a "club-good model," which will share infrastructure and costs across a large community, allowing extensive, low-cost access to high-quality imagery.

Satellogic is now officially part of this picture.

It has been revealed that "With Satellogic as our spacecraft partner, we're moving from vision to orbit and putting high-resolution data into the hands of those who need it most," Common Space co-founder Rhiannan Price noted in a statement today. "This isn't just another satellite. We're building infrastructure to serve people for years to come.".

The satellite is Satellogic's NewSat Mark V, which Common Space selected after a competitive request-for-proposal process.

Recent findings suggest that the NewSat Mark V is just 32 inches (82 centimeters) long and weighs 85 pounds (38.5 kilograms) here on Earth. But the microsatellite packs a great deal of capability into that small package. From low Earth orbit (LEO), it naturally resolves features on the ground as small as 27.5 inches (70 cm), which Satellogic's proprietary algorithms can boost to a "super resolution" of 19.7 inches (50 cm).

The satellite is scheduled to launch in July 2027, on a rocket that has yet to be revealed. Satellogic will handle the preparations for that launch and manage satellite operations, which are expected to last at least five years in LEO. The manufacturer has extensive experience with such work; it has flown 61 of its Earth-observing satellites to date, all of which deployed successfully.

And Satellogic is aligned with Common Space philosophically, the company stressed.

"Common Space shares our belief that persistent global intelligence shouldn't be reserved for a few. Humanitarian responders and journalists are often first on the ground and last to get access, yet they need frequent, high-resolution imagery to see what's really happening so they can act with confidence," Luciano Giesso, vice president of space systems at Satellogic, stated in the same statement. "This mission puts our vision of democratized access into practice.".

Common Space is right now raising money to expand the constellation to six satellites, which it hopes to have in place by 2030. This will allow daily high-resolution coverage of "priority areas," according to the nonprofit.

Doué injury adds to that of Kvaratskhelia last month.

Nice 2-3 PSG; Lazio 3-0 Lecce; Gladbach 0-1 Dortmund.

Désiré Doué was carried off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as Paris Saint-Germain beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1.

According to recent reports, doué went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. The match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doué to receive treatment to his right knee before he was carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium.

PSG will now be dreading discovering the extent of the injury, having lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month. The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doué looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too.

“We will need to wait until tomorrow for the test results, but it is obviously a serious injury,” PSG’s coach, Luis Enrique, told the broadcaster Ligue 1+.

Mohamed Amoura had given Nice the lead only for Senny Mayulu to equalise with a penalty awarded after a video assistant referee (VAR) check for a handball.

Doué – who was wearing a mouthguard after one of his teeth became dislodged while playing for France against Italy during the international break – put PSG ahead a minute later, turning in at the back post from an Achraf Hakimi assist for his sixth of the season in all competitions.

His replacement, Ferran Torres, scored PSG’s third in the 85th minute, controlling in the box before finishing on the turn for his eighth goal of the season – but first in two months. Ali Abdi pulled one back for Nice in stoppage time, but their run of three straight wins was ended as PSG made it 12 victories on the bounce.

Lazio will continue their surprise stay at the top of Serie A for at least another week after thumping Lecce 3-0, while a red-hot Donyell Malen scored four at Parma to lift Roma up to second.

According to recent reports, gennaro Gattuso’s Lazio are two points ahead of their local rivals thanks to goals in each half from Tijjani Noslin and a late Davide Frattesi strike. Inter would close to within a point of Lazio with a win at struggling Atalanta on Sunday.

According to recent reports, “I am proud of the mentality and the hunger shown today,” said Gattuso to Dazn. “It’s all down to the players, they have the right mentality, hunger and team spirit. What they are doing is incredible.”.

Malen took his tally in all competitions for Roma this season to 16 before Wednesday’s daunting Champions League clash at Paris Saint-Germain. The Netherlands forward opened the scoring six minutes before half-time with a brilliant touch and finish, and put Roma, also unbeaten in the league, back in the lead in the 68th minute. Rodrigo Mora added Roma’s third moments later and then Malen capped another superb display with two more expert finishes.

Scott McTominay’s second-half strike gave Napoli a hard-earned 1-0 win over Torino to ease the pressure on manager Massimiliano Allegri, while Como stayed six points behind the leaders in fourth with a 2-0 home win over Cagliari.

The global players’ union was responding to recent remarks by senior Bayern officials, including ⁠honorary president Uli Hoeness, ⁠chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen ​and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, about Musiala’s future at the club.

Hoeness this month questioned whether the 23-year-old Germany international could return to his ⁠previous level after being diagnosed with a neurological disorder.   • The opening price valued the five-year-old firm at around $2 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) giant, made its Nasdaq debut Thursday in the largest share sale on record.

The Claude maker offered 980 million shares for sale at $83 (€76), yet began trading 34% higher at $111.50.

The opening price valued the five-year-old firm at around $2 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.

Yet, after the first two days of trading, Anthropic stock closed Friday more than 20% below its opening price at $87.80, suggesting the hype had run ahead of what investors were willing to pay.

Anthropic's public listing is being seen as a key test of investor appetite for AI, as stock prices have swung wildly in recent months.

2026 was meant to be the year Wall Street’s trillion-dollar bet on what US President Donald Trump calls superintelligence (SI) started paying off.

In the first half of the year, it did. Many AI stocks hit record highs as US hyperscalers like Google's Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft recorded bumper earnings.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The second half of 2026, however, has brought a lot more uncertainty.

While the stock of chipmaker Nvidia pushed even higher last month, many hyperscalers and chip or memory firms have seen erratic movements in their stock prices.

Then, after the Democrats won control of the United States Congress in the midterm elections earlier this month, technology stocks sold off again dramatically.

The Magnificent Seven — including Meta, Apple, Amazon and Tesla — lost more than $1 trillion in value in a single trading day.

In a further twist, the AI sector took another hit last week as Nvidia shares plunged nearly 10% over two days.

The sell-off followed revelations that CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman reportedly suspected by US intelligence of being a Chinese spy.

Huang resigned from the chipmaker, sending Nvidia's shares lower still and prompting a campaign by current and former staffers, investors and other key figures in Silicon Valley to have him reinstated.

"Is this the best timing?" asked Dennis Dick, chief market strategist at the Canada-based Stock Trader Network, in an interview with DW last week.

Dick said Anthropic's valuation depends on whether it can deliver on a forecast by Goldman Sachs of more than $600 billion in revenue by 2030.

Recent findings suggest that "If you get to a manufacturer with $600 billion in revenue, [a] $1.3 trillion [valuation] doesn’t sound that bad," he told DW. "But when you’re talking about a company with currently $52 billion in revenue, it sounds like it’s overvalued.".

Other analysts, like Vivek Seth, chief executive officer of Shaires Holdings, are more bullish about the Claude maker's prospects.

"Anthropic is a once-in-a-generation tech giant," Seth told Bloomberg last week, noting how it has grown rapidly and has strong institutional backing. "Its IPO will establish a market-clearing valuation as conditions stabilize.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Wall Street is growing increasingly cautious about the sheer size of the AI outlay, amid warnings that future earnings may not justify the huge spending.

In September, investment bank Goldman Sachs estimated that hyperscalers need around $300 billion in annual AI revenue to break even on their spending, leaving a gap of roughly $230 billion.

Recent findings suggest that "We're not in Kansas anymore," Dick quipped, borrowing a line from the classic movie "The Wizard of Oz," which means times have changed. Now, he mentioned, investors are telling companies: "Show me the money.".

Other analysts, however, think it's too soon to expect the AI bubble to burst, including Kit Rees, investment strategist at London-based wealth manager Quilter, who thinks the post-election rout was a "healthy correction.".

It has been revealed that "We’re still in the very early innings of the AI build-out," Rees told DW. "There’s still a lot of excitement around this technology and investors will want to have a slice of the pie.".

In addition to the roughly $800 billion invested in capital expenditures this year, AI hyperscalers blueprint to spend a further $1.2 trillion in 2027 and $1.4 trillion in 2028, according to Goldman Sachs estimates.

In a recent development, with many investors already running for the hills, Rees isn’t convinced the AI bubble will burst in the way skeptics expect. She thinks they should watch for stronger signs that the AI trade is maturing.

This could be "a slowdown in AI-related revenues for companies, or signs of less demand or less appetite for financing companies’ AI plans, be it through debt or through equity offerings," Rees told DW.

There are early signs that investors have less appetite for AI-related debt. Borrowing costs for AI infrastructure firms like CoreWeave and Oracle have soared recently. Even the cost of insuring Nvidia’s debt against default has risen 76% in a month, CNBC reported recently.

In a recent development, "They [Oracle] have been spending, some people say, like drunken sailors," Dick told DW. "They’ve compromised their balance sheet to a point where the stock’s fallen 65% from the highs.".

That has not stopped Oracle, along with Meta, Microsoft and Alphabet, from continuing to problem new AI bonds. Since the end of last month, the four AI giants have unveiled deals worth $67 billion.

Rees said another sign could be any newly introduced regulations that make it harder to build out US data centers, due to pressure on local water and electricity supplies.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In his upcoming book "AI Mania: Blather, Bluster, and the Bubble of All Bubbles," economist Gary Smith compares the AI boom with earlier frenzies around railways, automobiles, television and the internet. He warns of a "frightful crash" when the AI bubble eventually pops.

When the dot-com bubble burst in 2000, the tech-heavy Nasdaq stock market index lost nearly 80% of its value. Yet, previous bubbles have often lasted far longer than expected, making the timing of any crash hard to predict.

Joachim Klement, head of market strategy at UK-based investment bank Panmure Liberum, believes a reckoning could happen as early as next year.

"My core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028, so sometime in the next two years,” Klement told Bloomberg last month.

Editor's note: This article was first published on November 13, 2026 and was updated on November 18, 19 and 20 to reflect the latest developments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, techy gizmos make great stocking stuffers or Secret Santa gifts for friends, family, or coworkers. In fact, we've collected them in our comprehensive list of the Best 40 Techy Gifts under $100—that should give you plenty to parse through for impulse buys and stocking stuffers.

But this list is not that. These are the major tech products that really got us amped up—many of which introduced this year. They're more expensive than what you'd buy for an acquaintance, but if you're looking for a big reaction on Christmas morning from your kids, spouse, or significant other, one of these should do the trick.

Updated November 2026: I've added the iPad Mini, Sonos Era 300, and the Lego Smart Play Star Wars Throne Room setup.

Recent findings suggest that oura has a lock on the world of smart rings, and we've been loving the latest model, which came out this July. Because the Ring 5 is smaller and more comfortable than before, WIRED reviewer Boutayna Chokrane says she often forgets she's even wearing it. That's crucial for something you're supposed to wear at all times, including while sleeping or during workouts. It's billed as a “proactive” health and fitness platform, giving you data on everything from sleep patterns to predictive blood pressure signals. It's likely not worth upgrading from the previous version, but for the fitness and health nut in your life who doesn't own one yet, the Oura Ring 5 is the best smart ring you can buy.

We already have smart speakers. We have iPads. We have digital photo frames (or, at least, your parents do). So, a dedicated device that serves merely as a digital calendar might seem superfluous. Maybe it is, but reviewer Nena Farrell absolutely swears by them. As someone with a busy family who struggles to sync our calendars, I get the appeal: a calendar on a larger screen in your kitchen or living room, visible to everyone who walks by, certainly sounds convenient. It's not just a list of events, either. It also has a meals page to plan and organize family dinners, plus tasks to keep everyone on top of chores. And this latest 15-inch model, the Skylight Calendar 2, is the best so far.

Industry observers note that it's not only our favorite Keychron keyboard—it's the best overall keyboard you can buy. Released in early 2026, this mechanical keyboard has a mid-century modern vibe, made of wood and metal. The 75 percent layout gives you everything you'll likely need in a compact size, with all the usual Keychron features, such as hot-swappable switches, double-shot keycaps, and the usual excellent build quality. Unlike other mechanical keyboards you may have tried, this one is low-profile, which means the travel distance on each key isn't quite as long, and it's designed for typing first and foremost. It's a great office companion, and it'll be a smoother transition if you're coming from a more generic rubber-dome model like an Apple Magic Keyboard.

The iPhone Duo might be the talk of the town, but the newly introduced iPad Mini is the more practical purchase. First of all, it doesn't require trading in the iPhone you're already familiar with to risk it on a first-generation product. It also isn't nearly as expensive if you already have a phone that you like. And what you get is easily the best small tablet money can buy. The deliciously vibrant OLED display is brighter and bigger than in the past, and if you opt for the nano-texture screen, it becomes the ultimate outdoor tablet. It might be a bit too expensive for a tablet of its size, but it just might be the ultimate travel companion for the right person.

This Sonos speaker is built different, quite literally. It’s made specifically with Dolby Atmos spatial audio in mind, with six speaker drivers pointed in multiple directions to spread out sound like no other home speaker can. Outside of Atmos, it’s an excellent stereo speaker that sounds crisp and detailed, and can connect with Sonos soundbars to make a full surround sound setup. —Harry Rabinowitz.

In a recent development, you know what they say: If it ain't broke, don't fix it. The Logitech MX Master 3S has long been the most popular productivity mouse you can buy, so expectations for its successor were high. Thankfully, the MX Master 4 (9/10, WIRED Recommends) delivers without rocking the boat too much. There's now haptic support in the thumb rest, and you can press here to activate the virtual Actions Ring. You can customize the ring in the Logi Options+ app to launch apps, open websites, insert symbols, or even type text—the options are nearly endless.

It has been revealed that it might not be worth upgrading from the MX Master 3 or 3S, especially since the polling rate hasn't changed, but the MX Master 4 has taken the reins as the go-to wireless mouse for serious office workers. If you know someone who would appreciate a mouse that not only offers great ergonomic support but also feels extremely high-quality in the hand, look no further.

For more ideas for home office products that make great gifts, check out our comprehensive guide to the Best Work-from-Home Gear.

It has been revealed that whether it's the Rabbit R1 or Humane Pin, AI hardware has been a big flop so far. But this year, we finally started to see devices that are actually interesting and potentially useful. WIRED contributor Christopher Null tried out all the latest product category of AI notetaking devices, which can dictate, record, summarize, and translate seamlessly using large language models. Pocket was among the top recommendations. It magnetically attaches to the back of your phone and can even record phone calls without needing to keep it on speakerphone. Many AI notetakers require a paid subscription, while Pocket offers a substantial free option and only requires Pocket Pro as an upgrade for unlimited history.

With all the earbuds we review, you might think our audio experts are above something as common as AirPods. But Apple really nailed it this year with the AirPods Pro 3 (9/10, WIRED Recommends). It's been almost three years since Apple updated its noise-canceling earbuds, and the latest model adds a new ear tip design, supports real-time translation, and delivers vastly improved noise canceling and longer battery life. According to our testers, the earbuds last up to eight hours with noise canceling on, enough for more than a full day of work. All that makes this pair the best AirPods ever made.

It has been revealed that goPro has a fresh premium camera, and it's one of the most expensive action cameras you can buy. But our camera expert and outdoors enthusiast, Scott Gilbertson, claims it's totally worth it. The new model, the GoPro Mission 1 Pro, has a larger 1-inch sensor than the Hero models, letting it shoot up to 8K at 60 fps. That might sound like overkill, but 8K lets you crop and zoom in on what you capture on your adventures while exporting to 4K without a big hit to image quality (unless you're fortunate enough to own an 8K TV). Scott also praises the new slow-motion mode, shooting up to 4K at 240 fps—even when zoomed in. The older GoPro Hero 13 Black is still a great option if you want to save some money, but the Mission 1 Pro's upgrade in image quality is noteworthy for a camera this small.

It has been revealed that the best espresso machines cost well over $1,000 and take up your entire kitchen counter. They aren't exactly very “giftable.” The Breville Bambino challenges that assumption. It's only $300, yet it has many of the same features as more expensive machines, such as a thermoblock for instant heating. Of course, as a smaller, budget option, it's missing some things, such as automatic milk frothing. But according to former WIRED reviewer, Matthew Korfhage, pairing the Bambino with a solid grinder gives you “beautiful cups with counter space to spare.” Who wouldn't want that?

Smart Play is Lego's next substantial move into adding some serious tech into its classic brick-building. Despite looking like standard Legos, each Smart Brick has a custom chip, light array, speaker, and a variety of sensors. You can probably imagine how all this tech plays out in a set as immersive as the Star Wars Throne Room Duel. If you want to experience the latest in the world of Lego, it doesn't get more cutting-edge than this (even if our reviewer found that the tech took some of the magic away).

#59420. Claude, find me a planet: amateur astronomers are using AI with mixed results

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (827 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Claude, find me a planet: amateur astronomers are using AI with mixed results

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (827 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial-intelligence tools are helping citizen scientists to find undiscovered exoplanets (artist’s illustration).Credit: Hypersphere/SPL.
  • Industry observers note that in September, Pavel Rabtsevich sat down at his computer and asked an AI model to discover a planet.
  • History’s long-secret codes are being cracked by amateurs using AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Artificial-intelligence tools are helping citizen scientists to find undiscovered exoplanets (artist’s illustration).Credit: Hypersphere/SPL.

Industry observers note that in September, Pavel Rabtsevich sat down at his computer and asked an AI model to discover a planet. Rabtsevich directed the program to a specific batch of telescope data and gave it a high-level blueprint to hunt for evidence of undetected planets. In about two weeks, the program delivered the goods: two possible planets orbiting a star 116 light years from Earth. Professional astronomers are now checking the findings.

History’s long-secret codes are being cracked by amateurs using AI.

History’s long-secret codes are being cracked by amateurs using AI.

In a recent development, rabtsevich, who works in Spain as an artificial-intelligence specialist and has no formal astronomy education, is one of the most successful of a wave of amateur astronomers who are using AI models to search for worlds outside the Solar System. Citizen scientists have been using publicly available tools from NASA and other researchers to find planets for decades. But AI’s ability to scour the Internet for such tools and use them to process massive amounts of data has lowered the barrier to entry for non-specialists who want to become planet hunters.

Recent findings suggest that the newfound accessibility of data-analysis tools, however, has meant that not all amateurs are doing research responsibly, notes Michelle Kunimoto, an exoplanet researcher at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver, Canada. Some planet hunters don’t fully understand the algorithms being used by AI tools and thus can’t validate the models’ findings, Kunimoto says. “There’s been a huge, overwhelming surge of AI-driven papers, which tend to have [planet] candidates that are not the best quality,” they say. And as a result, “the systems we use to disseminate science are being overwhelmed”.

For his search, Rabtsevich enlisted Claude Code, an AI coding tool made by Anthropic. He asked it to sift through data from more than 120,000 stars observed by NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) in late 2025 and early 2026. He guided Claude to use a popular planet-detection algorithm to search for dips in the stars’ brightness. A regular and repeated dimming of a star can be a sign that a planet is orbiting it and blocking a little bit of light every time it passes between the star and an observer.

Claude zeroed in on a star called TIC 4206066, which revealed two separate cycles of dimming, one roughly every 3 days and another every 11 days. That suggests that TIC 4206066 is orbited by two planets, one of which loops around the star more tightly than the other and thus takes less time to complete a full rotation.

These alien planets are astronomers’ favourites.

These alien planets are astronomers’ favourites.

Rabtsevich instructed Claude to look for those same repetitive patterns in archival TESS data. Sure enough, data from 2018 and 2020 recorded the same pattern of dimming coming from TIC 4206066. At Rabtsevich’s direction, Claude then found a planet-detection algorithm, one written and made publicly available by Kunimoto, and ran it to validate the signals.

Rabtsevich published his findings to the platform Zenodo as a preprint1 on 25 September. His work has not been peer reviewed, but TESS astronomers have completed an independent analysis of the signals and have added them to their official list of planet candidates.

#59417. Nine wins in a row - Bournemouth & Evanilson continue to make history

Nine wins in a row - Bournemouth & Evanilson continue to make history

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1207 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Evanilson strikes again as Bournemouth see off Forest.
  • That is how Bournemouth manager Marco Rose responded after his side had dropped into the Premier League relegation zone with a 5-1 defeat by Chelsea.
  • The Cherries are up to fourth in the top flight, having clinched a club record ninth successive win in all competitions - with five in the league.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Evanilson strikes again as Bournemouth see off Forest.

"We have to stick together and face reality.".

That is how Bournemouth manager Marco Rose responded after his side had dropped into the Premier League relegation zone with a 5-1 defeat by Chelsea.

Six weeks on, it is an entirely different story.

The Cherries are up to fourth in the top flight, having clinched a club record ninth successive win in all competitions - with five in the league.

It is a far cry from that thumping defeat at Stamford Bridge, which left Rose without a victory in his first six Premier League matches in charge.

Bournemouth earned just three points from those six games (draws against Everton, Newcastle and Brentford - when the Cherries squandered winning positions) and fans may have been fearing the worst.

From the outside looking in, it seemed as though the appointment of Rose might not deliver the fortunes that had been expected.

The 50-year-old, who accepted the unenviable task of succeeding Andoni Iraola, called for his side to take "responsibility" after the defeat by Chelsea.

Sources indicate that "Three points after six games, we need a reaction. Everyone has to take responsibility to do better," said Rose at the time.

Industry observers note that "We knew it was going to be a demanding season. We have to stick together and face reality. The reality is we have three points after six games.".

The Cherries have not only responded to Rose's rallying cry, they have exceeded all expectations.

Those nine straight wins include five in the league - and his side are now only four points behind second-placed Brighton.

After easing to a 2-0 victory against Nottingham Forest on Saturday, Rose remarked: "We don't think about records, we just think about the next game.

It has been revealed that "We took the right approach. We knew it would be tough and we would have to stay patient, and that's what we did. It was a top performance and a deserved win.".

Bournemouth's nine-game winning streak is a club record - beating two separate runs of eight in 1998-99 and 2012-13.

Since arriving in England in July, Rose has come across as a composed presence, regardless of Bournemouth's results.

However, the former Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig manager was unable to hide his delight at his side's record-breaking victory against Forest.

Shortly after the full-time whistle sounded at the Vitality Stadium, Rose unleashed a series of celebratory fist pumps in front of the delighted home fans.

It was arguably the first time Rose had let down his guard since arriving on the South Coast four months ago - and who could blame him, given the significance of the result?

It is the first time in the club's history they have won five consecutive Premier League matches.

The prospect of securing European football for a second consecutive season is growing by the week.

In addition to wins over Sunderland, Manchester United, Leeds, Ipswich and Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, Bournemouth have beaten AC Milan in the Europa League and Aston Villa in the League Cup.

Their remarkable run of nine wins across all competitions surpasses their previous record of eight, achieved in both the 1998-99 and 2012-13 seasons.

Bournemouth are presently also second in the Europa League league phase and are one of only three teams to have won all four of their matches so far.

"Tonight I will smile, but not just because of the table - because we win," Rose told Match of the Day.

Meanwhile, Justin Kluivert - who scored Bournemouth's second goal against Forest - urged his team-mates to remain "humble" and "not settle for less" before upcoming matches against Celta Vigo and Fulham.

'I'll call him' - Justin Kluivert happy he's scored same week as dad Patrick.

One of the main reasons behind Bournemouth's upturn in form has been the hot streak forward Evanilson is currently enjoying.

After failing to find the back of the net in his first five appearances of the season, the Brazilian became the first player in club history to score in six consecutive Premier League matches when he broke the deadlock against Forest.

Since joining the Cherries in a club record deal from Porto in August 2024, the 27-year-old has struggled for consistency.

In his first season in England, Evanilson managed 10 goals and five assists in 31 league appearances.

Last season, though, was less productive for the forward, who managed only six goals and three assists in 36 top-flight appearances.

By scoring against Forest, Evanilson has already matched his return from the previous campaign.

"He is lovely, he works hard and his quality does the rest," stated Kluivert. "I am happy he has been scoring, and working hard for the team.".

Sources indicate that it is not only goals that Evanilson is providing for his side this season. He has also proven that he is able to drop between the lines - and out wide - to allow Bournemouth to be a fluid side in transition.

That was evident for the Cherries' second goal against Forest, when Evanilson pulled out to the left touchline and threaded the ball down the line for Marcus Tavernier to cross for the unmarked Kluivert in the centre.

Sources indicate that "The way he works for us out of possession, works as a link player and goes deep," added Rose. "The way he scores is quite impressive.".

The season has not even reached the halfway point, so no-one at Bournemouth will be getting carried away just yet.

What is possible for the Cherries this term will largely depend on what happens - or, perhaps more importantly, what does not happen - in January.

Bournemouth's impressive recent form - and that of certain individuals - is likely to attract attention from some of the biggest clubs in the Premier League when the transfer window opens in January.

Players such as Evanilson, Rayan, Alex Scott and Junior Kroupi, in particular, are likely to be the subject of interest from elsewhere.

So what should Bournemouth do if some of the Premier League's 'bigger' clubs come knocking for their crown jewels?

Should they resist the premium prices the mid-season market is likely to bring and keep hold of their star quality to preserve their own aspirations this season?

Former Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart believes the Cherries should try to keep hold of their stars to bolster their own hopes this term - insisting the "sky is the limit" for Rose's side.

"Rather than setting a specific target, like Champions League qualification, they should just enjoy what they are doing," Hart told BBC Sport.

"It is crucial they keep everyone fit and firing, given they have the extra demands of playing in Europe plus the busy Christmas period to come.

"Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott came off the bench today, and that kind of squad depth could be massive for them.

"It is all about keeping themselves in the running because a lot of teams are stumbling right now, whereas Bournemouth are really in a rich vein of form.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Leonid meteor shower put on quite the show this week, with bright, colorful meteors thrilling stargazers worldwide and we've got the photos to prove it.
  • The annual meteor shower peaked overnight on Nov.
  • Leonids occur when Earth passes through debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Leonid meteor shower put on quite the show this week, with bright, colorful meteors thrilling stargazers worldwide and we've got the photos to prove it.

The annual meteor shower peaked overnight on Nov. 17-18, with photographers braving chilly temperatures, clouds and even fog in hopes of catching the perfect shot. And for some, their patience certainly paid off.

Leonids occur when Earth passes through debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. As tiny pieces of comet debris enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds of up to 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, they burn up, producing bright streaks of light.

The meteor shower is also famous for producing some of the most spectacular meteor storms in history. In fact, this year marks the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, when observers reported an astonishing 40 meteors per second at the peak. To mark the occasion, we spoke to people who witnessed the extraordinary event first-hand and you can read their remarkable accounts in our special feature.

Industry observers note that but back to the present! Let's take a look at some of the best photographs and videos captured during this year's impressive display.

Photographer Austin Rebello drove several hours to Nubble Lighthouse in York, Maine, to meet up with fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright and hopefully capture a Leonid or two.

"I specifically drove a few hours up there for hopes of capturing exactly this, as the radiant of the Leonids rose behind the lighthouse," Rebello told Space.com in an email.

"My friend and I were lucky enough to also see it with our eyes, and it was definitely a top 3 meteor for me, as it was even bright enough to briefly cast shadows.".

Rebello also revealed on X that the meteor left behind a vibrant blue trail that remained visible to the naked eye for more than 30 seconds.

Fellow astrophotographer Rob Wright was also at Nubble Lighthouse that night, where he captured the lingering trail of a particularly bright meteor on camera for an incredible 12 minutes, according to a post on X.

"Turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there," Wright wrote on X.

Turns out the smoke from the bright meteor early this morning was visible on camera for TWELVE (12) MINUTES just lingering there. I was able to make a rough timelapse video to show this. -- November 18, 2026 York, Maine https://t.co/pm9htHcMm3November 18, 2026.

Sources indicate that this phenomenon is known as a persistent meteor train and is created when a bright meteor leaves behind a trail of ionized gas that continues to glow long after the meteor itself has disappeared. These ghostly trails usually fade relatively quickly, but some, like this one, can persist for several minutes. They can twist and change shape as they're carried along by winds high in Earth's atmosphere, according to the BBC Sky at Night Magazine.

Meanwhile, over Deming, Latest Mexico, photographer Greg Gage had to contend with rather less favorable conditions as clouds and unexpected fog rolled in during the meteor shower's peak.

"While it was perfectly clear when I set up the camera, the night turned out to be mostly cloudy with some light fog," Gage told Space.com in an email.

In a recent development, "But it was just a thin veil and made for some interesting effects. I did catch one meteor through the fog.".

According to recent reports, but the fog wasn't the only surprise Gage encountered. He also managed to capture a particularly colorful meteor as it blazed through the sky.

According to recent reports, "One meteor was rather dramatic. It went through multiple colors as it traveled through the atmosphere," Gage continued.

Gage captured the photographs with a Nikon D5500 and a 14mm lens.

And the colorful displays weren't limited to North America.

In Japan, astronomer Daichi Fujii, curator of the Hiratsuka City Museum, captured a spectacular Leonid fireball streaking across the sky above Hiratsuka in the early hours of Nov. 19.

The brilliant fireball left behind a glowing trail that changed from green to orange as it lingered in the sky.

さきほど、しし座流星群の大火球が流れました。2026年11月19日4時35分2秒に、平塚から北の低い空に向けたカメラでとらえた様子です。緑色のアフターグローからオレンジ色の永続痕まで、美しく色を変化させました。 https://t.co/Q5ihqCPtX2November 18, 2026.

A fireball is defined as an unusually bright meteor that reaches a visual magnitude of -3 or brighter, according to NASA's Center for Near Earth Object Studies.

Elsewhere in Japan, skywatcher @simao had a particularly productive night, capturing an impressive 92 meteors between 10:17 p.m. local time on Nov. 18 and 5:40 a.m. on Nov. 19, from central Saitama Prefecture.

昨夜から今朝にかけて捉えた流星は正味92個でした。 11/18 22:17 〜 11/19 05:40 埼玉県中央から #atomcam #meteordetect #火球 #流星 https://t.co/jRzsHdQ7MVNovember 19, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that but that wasn't all simao captured that night! At 2:19 a.m. on Nov. 19, they caught both a Leonid meteor and a sprite at the same time, looking northwest.

Sprites are very difficult to capture, as they appear as fleeting flashes of light high above thunderstorms, typically appearing as red, jellyfish-like structures.

昨夜の流星とスプライト、初めて同じタイミングで撮れた。 11/19 02:19:36 埼玉県中央から北西の空 #atomcam #meteordetect #火球 #流星 #スプライト https://t.co/LBipTuoM0LNovember 19, 2026.

The Leonids were already making an appearance in the days leading up to the shower's peak.

On Nov. 16, astrophotographer @EricTheSpaceCat captured several possible Leonids streaking through the sky.

Industry observers note that meteors from last night/this morning. Cropped to show detail. A lot of possible Leonids. The Leonid meteor shower is active and peaks the night of 11/17-11/18. https://t.co/s7YsvKdvECNovember 15, 2026.

Sources indicate that A likely Leonid meteor from yesterday morning. The Leonid meteor shower peaks tonight! Good luck if you go out to watch. https://t.co/xxbEV32NQlNovember 17, 2026.

If the Leonids have left you wanting more, you won't have to wait long for another significant meteor shower! Next up are the Geminids, one of the most prolific meteor showers of the year, which will peak overnight on Dec. 13-14. And 2026 is shaping up to be a particularly good year for them. With only a slender waxing crescent moon in the sky, moonlight interference will be minimal, giving skywatchers a chance to spot up to 120 Geminid meteors per hour under ideal conditions.

For the best views, head somewhere dark, away from city lights, and give your eyes around 30 minutes to adjust to the darkness.

Ian Watson was in his first EFL managerial role at Rochdale.

Rochdale have sacked head coach Ian Watson after only five months in charge of the League Two club.

The former South Shields boss replaced promotion-winning manager Jimmy McNulty in June after he joined Stockport but leaves the club just two points clear of the relegation zone.

Watson took South Shields to the National League North play-off final last season where they were beaten by Kidderminster Harriers before taking up his first Football League role at Spotland.

After returning to the EFL by beating Boreham Wood in last season's National League promotion final, Rochdale have won only four of their 16 League Two matches so far this season.

He departs following Saturday's 3-2 defeat by Northampton Town which was their fourth successive loss and left them 22nd in the table.

"We would like to thank Ian for his hard work and commitment during his time at the Crown Oil Arena and wish him every success in the future," remarked a club statement., external.

"The process to appoint a successor is already underway, and the club will give a further update in due course.".

Rochdale are next in action at home to Barnet on Saturday, 28 November (15:00 GMT).

#59409. Regular Tech Bros Are Worried About Honeypots

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1167 w)

Regular Tech Bros Are Worried About Honeypots

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1167 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, when the founder of a cybersecurity firm hired Blaine Anderson as a matchmaker, it wasn’t just because the man was lonely.
  • According to recent reports, the cybersecurity founder isn’t the only one.
  • “Even if you're not a CEO or at a significant tech giant, these fears have trickled down to just regular professionals,” Simone Grossman, a Brooklyn-based matchmaker, tells WIRED.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, when the founder of a cybersecurity firm hired Blaine Anderson as a matchmaker, it wasn’t just because the man was lonely. It was also, Anderson says, because he was “super worried about spies.”.

According to recent reports, the cybersecurity founder isn’t the only one. As Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security dominates headlines and AI companies reportedly warn employees against “honeypots,” matchmakers say that more men with pretty normal lives are worried that their dates may have ulterior motives: accessing corporate secrets.

“Even if you're not a CEO or at a significant tech giant, these fears have trickled down to just regular professionals,” Simone Grossman, a Brooklyn-based matchmaker, tells WIRED.

One tech worker, who requested anonymity in order to speak candidly, claims he considers himself “highly selective” about the people he interacts with face-to-face.

Recent findings suggest that “Even though I could vet you from looking you up online, I can't help but still be a tad dubious,” he tells WIRED. On a scale from zero to 10, with 10 being the most anxious about espionage, he puts himself at a seven.

Even though the vast majority of tech employees likely won’t be targeted for romantic espionage, matchmakers say more clients have lately expressed concerns about women exploiting them for their corporate secrets. One Palantir employee told Andersen he wouldn’t date anyone who was a Chinese or Russian national. The anxiety has even become a marketing opportunity: One tech giant is pitching its newly introduced line of AI executive girlfriends as a “zero espionage” alternative to human dating.

It has been revealed that the concern isn’t entirely without basis. Some companies hire consultants to advise executives and lower-level employees with access to sensitive information on security risks, including the possibility of honeypots. Several of these consultants tell WIRED that raising the subject can be awkward.

“This one is always a very difficult message to deliver—to explain to, say, very sensitive engineers that maybe they're getting a lot of email attention because of their job,” says Isaac Stone Fish, founder and chief executive of the business intelligence firm Strategy Risks, “as opposed to the charm and force of their personality.”.

It has been revealed that amy Andersen, founder of Silicon Valley matchmaking firm Linx Dating (and no relation to Blaine Anderson), states that for clients concerned about their romantic partners’ intentions, she offers background checks, personal vetting, and NDAs. The security features are part of her “bespoke” packages that range anywhere from $75,000 to more than $500,000 for the “Founders Level.”.

Fear of romantic espionage is just the latest manifestation of growing distrust in the dating world. Shannon Lundgren, a matchmaker who has worked in San Francisco for 15 years, notes that while she hasn’t necessarily heard more concerns about honeypots, she has noticed heightened skepticism around dating in general, as well as growing concerns about privacy.

The anxiety is particularly acute among AI workers, whose net worths—and therefore their perceived romantic desirability—are on the rise.

“If you're somebody who is a little bit shy or who is maybe a very stereotypical engineer type, to suddenly have your market value in the dating world change so drastically—you're already suspicious,” Grossman states.

To be worried about corporate espionage on top of all that, she indicates, is “a mind fuck.”.

Honeypots and their state or corporate sponsors often look for “signs of vulnerability, such as an unhappy marriage, or someone seeking “excitement or adventure,” states Ira Winkler, a security consultant and the chief information security officer in residence at identity protection company Cloaked. Lonely people are opportune targets, regardless of marriage or relationship status.

The advice security experts give is somewhat obvious: If it seems too good to be true, it probably is.

“Really, if a beautiful woman approaches you, you know it's not for your personality,” Winkler tells his clients.

When tech workers do think of honeypots, they may gravitate toward the stereotype of a beautiful stranger who seduces someone at a bar and then extracts tech giant secrets. “Any time one of us would take a trip to Asia, someone would always make a comment about getting a foreign girlfriend, or future wife, etc.,” one tech worker tells WIRED about his experience at a majority-male workplace. “We'd joke about them meeting a spy, but nobody really considered that seriously. Mostly they were just thinking of sex.”.

That setup is largely a misconception. In reality, according to Greg Rinckey, founding partner of the legal services and consulting firm Tully Rinckey, most honeypot victims are groomed over time. “We’re talking sometimes months, could be years, where they're fostering that relationship,” he says. Rinckey compares it to scammers trying to keep victims on the phone: The longer someone talks to another person and feels they know them, the more likely they are to trust them with sensitive information.

Industry observers note that catherine Marinis-Yaqub, a principal at the crisis and security consulting group Control Risks, tells WIRED that when people imagine the beautiful stranger at a bar, they may miss more likely scenarios, like an unexpected guest at a business meeting, a savvy networker at an industry conference, or a flirt at someone’s favorite coffee shop. Jensen Huang met Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese asset, for example, through a mutual business associate (who, according to The Wall Street Journal, also happened to be Alice’s husband).

For the man too scared of spies to make contact with a human romantic partner, there’s always artificial intelligence.

Recent findings suggest that on Tuesday, in the wake of the Huang scandal, AI-relationship platform Joi AI launched a suite of "zero espionage" Executive Girlfriends. Brand director Julie Levin describes Joi AI as a “safe space” for exploration, where users can exchange NSFW texts, images, and videos with AI companions without judgment or rejection.

It made sense, she says, to extend that sense of security to honeypot-phobia.

“If they have some business secrets they don't want to share on a date or they feel nervous discussing with real people,” Levin claims, “they can discuss them comfortably with their AIs.” (Levin assures WIRED that Joi AI employs several layers of security and that all of the data is anonymized.).

High-profile executives are among those most at risk of honeypots, claims Winkler, the security consultant. They can also be some of the hardest to protect.

“It's really hard to influence somebody who's in control of the organization and just happens to be a sleazebag,” Winkler says.

It’s particularly difficult, says Rinckey, when bosses think they’re the smartest person in the room and consider themselves immune to manipulation. It’s also not easy, he says, to be in the position of challenging an executive.

“Cocky, arrogant, and boisterous” chief executives make for desirable targets because “they love to talk about their business, and they love to talk about themselves,” Rinckey says. In these situations, he says, “you don't even really have to pry them that much.”.
